text: {"standards":[{"code":"L.6.1","verdict":"partly","reason":"Part C's quick write and the Part B think-pair-share ask students to write complete sentences with agreement and present tense, but the lesson only has the teacher check grammar and gives no direct instruction in conventions."},{"code":"L.6.4","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the Break the Words Apart activity, students work out meanings of unknown words like restrained and interjected by analyzing root, prefix, and suffix alongside context clues."},{"code":"RL.6.2","verdict":"taught","reason":"In Part B, students state the resolution, separate a plot summary from opinion, and name a theme (family loyalty) with a supporting detail from the chapter."},{"code":"RL.6.3","verdict":"partly","reason":"Part A and Part B trace how Zeus, Poseidon, and Percy respond and how the conflict resolves, but no activity has students describe how the plot unfolds across a series of episodes."},{"code":"RL.6.6","verdict":"taught","reason":"In Part C, students annotate how Percy's first-person narration and modern attitude shape what readers notice and think about Zeus and Poseidon, and imagine a distant past-tense narrator."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"uses","reason":"The lesson's Launch, Literacy Lab, and Learning in Action activities all direct students to The Lightning Thief, Chapter 21, pp. 344–353, matching the Outline's named text and pages."}}
